observations: All three paths produced identical public Compact snapshots and results after every measured turn.
Across the 10-turn fixture, both play-turn paths reduced Node starts from 30 to 10 and measured wall time by about 46 percent.
Peak exit RSS was 12.3 MB higher for interactive and 30.3 MB higher for finite plan than legacy single-step; retained Runtime and same-process temporary allocations contribute to this peak.

Within this 10-turn measurement, interactive exit RSS changed from 149.7 MB to 152.2 MB and finite-plan exit RSS fell from 170.6 MB to 158.7 MB. This is evidence of no large cumulative growth over the measured range, not a general memory bound.
The supplementary post-history-fix one-turn run measured interactive exit RSS 3.1 MB below legacy and finite-plan exit RSS 1.9 MB above legacy, with lower external memory in both new paths.
Caches, input lines, request counts, finite plans, and output writes have explicit implementation bounds; the OS measurements above report observed process behavior separately.
